subject: Snapshot retention offset amendment request - AtlasCare
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <security@atlascare.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarification on backup purge timeline and temporary hold option

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking this — quick background: AtlasCare is preparing for a data migration and we need a temporary extension to the backup purge window while the migration is validated. Our DPA calls for a 30-day restoreability period after deletion, but our legal team is asking if Redwood can provide a 60-day recovery offset for the next two months for a single tenant (AtlasCare) while we complete cutover and forensic checks.

Can you confirm:
- What the current backup purge cadence is (snapshots, weekly/monthly teeth)
- Whether Redwood can set a tenant-level snapshot hold or offset the purge for 60 days
- Any controls/attestations you can provide (SOC 2 evidence, subprocessors, cross-border transfer notes)

Attached: attestation_request.pdf (high-level checklist legal requested).

We'd appreciate a quick call if helpful — legal@atlascare.com is on copy.

Best,
Elena
Security Lead, AtlasCare
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <security@atlascare.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarification on backup purge timeline and temporary hold option

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Kimberly (Compliance) and Priyom (Persistence/Runbook) to align the legal and operational sides. Quick summary of how Redwood currently handles deletions and backups:

- Deletion workflow: user-initiated deletes mark objects with a tombstone immediately; logical indices are removed within minutes, but the underlying data lives in immutable snapshots for an additional retention window determined by the account policy.
- Snapshots & purge cadence: we take incremental snapshots every 6 hours and a full snapshot weekly (Sunday 03:00 UTC). Snapshot purge jobs run weekly with cross-region coordination; default backup retention is 45 days for hosted accounts.
- Tenant-level holds: we do support tenant-scoped snapshot holds (temporary hold flag) which prevents the purge job from removing snapshots for that tenant even if they fall outside the default retention window.
- Subprocessors & transfers: backups in hosted mode are stored on our cloud object store and are replicated to a single DR region; subprocessors (listed in our DPA) have read-limited access only for restoration workflows. Cross-border transfer depends on region selection — we can confine backups to a single region if requested.
- Evidence: we can provide SOC 2 exported artifacts and the signed subprocessor list; will need a normal request via compliance@redwood.com.

Operationally, we can:
1) place a tenant-scoped 60-day hold on AtlasCare snapshots for a defined two-month window;
2) produce a short attestation deck for legal covering the hold and subprocessors;
3) provide a runbook snippet for the restore process and expected RTO (see Priyom).

Priyom — can you sketch the run-of-show and cost delta (approx) for a 60-day hold for that tenant? Kimberly — is there a compliance signoff template we should use for the addendum?

Rachel Kim
Head of Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Elena Martinez <security@atlascare.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarification on backup purge timeline and temporary hold option

Hi all — quick compliance note:

- DPA: Under our standard DPA we commit to reasonable technical and organisational measures and publish our subprocessor list. A 60-day temporary hold is outside the default retention but is contractually feasible if documented as an addendum or via a short-term exception.
- Requirements from AtlasCare: for an exception we typically ask for (1) a signed addendum referencing the retention offset, (2) an authorized legal contact for change control (legal@atlascare.com should suffice), and (3) confirmation of whether the hold should be region-constrained (EU-only vs. global).
- Evidence package: I can pull SOC 2 export artifacts and the subprocessor access logs for restoration actions; these are provided under a compliance request ticket.

If AtlasCare confirms the legal contact and region scoping, we can greenlight the exception pending finance signoff for increased storage costs.

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Compliance & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Elena Martinez <security@atlascare.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 10:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarification on backup purge timeline and temporary hold option

Elena/Rachel/Kimberly — operational detail and cost estimate below.

Runbook (high level):
- Step 0: Accept signed addendum and ticketing approval (Compliance).
- Step 1: Create tenant-scoped hold flag in the snapshot index (id: hold-atlascare-202702).
- Step 2: Mark all incremental and weekly snapshots for the tenant as exempt from the next 8 purge cycles.
- Step 3: Track held bytes on the customer billing dashboard; finance will create a temporary invoice line for extra snapshot storage.
- Step 4: After the two-month window, execute a coordinated purge unless AtlasCare requests extension. A full restore drill can be scheduled within 48 hours for verification.

Cost: approximate additional storage delta ~ 1.2 TB * $0.02/GB-month => ~$24/month (example numbers; final will be per-account).

I can enact the hold within 48 hours of receiving the signed addendum and ticket ID; I will attach the runbook snippet for audit.

Attachment: snapshot_hold_runbook.md (run commands and ACL notes).

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Product Operations, Persistence
Redwood Inference

Thanks — that all sounds good. Our legal team will send a signed addendum to legal@redwood.com today; region: US-only. Please proceed once you have the signed doc. We'll also request the SOC 2 exports and subprocessor list via the compliance ticket you mentioned.

Could you also confirm the exact purge job that will be skipped and the time window so our engineers can plan validation runs? If you can include the runbook snippet in the compliance ticket that will be perfect.

Appreciate the quick coordination.

—Elena
